steps.text: Whisk Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, teriyaki sauce, molasses, and liquid smoke together in a bowl until molasses has dissolved; whisk in canola oil, sesame seeds, brown sugar, minced garlic, paprika, garlic salt, and garlic pepper.
Pour marinade into a resealable plastic bag. Add chicken thighs, coat with marinade, squeeze out excess air, and seal the bag. Marinate in the refrigerator for 4 hours.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat and lightly oil the grate.
Remove chicken from marinade; shake off excess. Discard remaining marinade.

Cook chicken on the preheated grill until no longer pink and the juices run clear, about 12 minutes per side. An instant-read thermometer inserted into centers should read at least 165 degrees F (75 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Delectable Marinated Chicken Thighs
raw_recipe.description: This marinated chicken thighs recipe is easy to prep with a sweet and smoky marinade of molasses, garlic, paprika, soy and teriyaki sauce before grilling.

video.description: Teriyaki sauce is the key to this delectable marinade for chicken thighs.

review.reviewBody: Oh my goodness! This stuff is great. I made mostly as written...never buy garlic salt or garlic pepper, so just added salt/pepper and more garlic (probably at least twice the called for amount). Only marinated the 4 hours and did on the grill. My 13 year old son just devoured it! Will make again and hopefully marinade even longer next time. Served with grilled pineapple and rice

We all know how good this marinade is so this comment is mainly for me and others who use a Traeger. I cut the oil by 2/3 of the recipe. Traeger at 450', chicken on 8-10 min (flipping halfway through). While the chicken is on, bring the remaining marinade to a boil then simmer for 5 min. Once chicken is done, bathe it in the marinade once more before putting it back on the grill for a final 5 min. SO FREGGIN MOIST AND DELICIOUS.

The title for this recipe perfectly describes how this dish turned out! Even my pickiest eater loved it! I did not have molasses so I used honey instead. I didn't have garlic pepper so I simply used black pepper. I added a tsp. of onion powder as I use this for almost all of my marinades and dry rubs. I also added two tbsp. of the juice from my canned pineapples that I grilled along with this and one tsp of grated ginger. I believe that the liquid smoke is probably the secret ingredient in this recipe and I would strongly suggest not omitting it!! I only had chicken breasts so I cubed and skewered them, grilling them for a total of 24 minutes. I was only able to marinate the chicken for about 2 1/2 hours but the chicken still turned out tasty and juicy. This is one of the best recipes I have found for chicken and will try this again with other meats.

I wasn't expecting much but needed a quick marinade. This was fabulous! I skipped the sesame seeds and instead used about 1 tsp. toasted sesame oil (I was afraid the seeds would burn on the grill), used 1 hefty tsp. garlic powder and ommitted minced garlic & garlic pepper. I added only about 2 Tbs. of canola oil and cubed the chicken for kebabs then marinated for about 4 hours. It absorbed the marinade and wasn't too smoky (I'm not a huge liquid smoke fan but used the full tsp. per other reviewers). I'll absolutely make this again. Next time I'll boil the extra marinade for 3 minutes and serve alongside.

Loved this recipe! Mostly because I had nearly everything already in my refrigerator and pantry, except molasses. So I used honey instead and followed the rest of the recipe exactly. The chicken thighs were amazing and I only marinated them for about 2 1/2 hours. I served them with a vegetable stir fry of broccoli, red pepper, red onion, and mushrooms with a light drizzle of hoisin sauce. It was super healthy and delicious. Will be making these again.

Did not have teriyaki sauce, and instead of paprika we like the hotter "sambal oelek" chilies! added about a teaspoon of that to the marinade...only had it in the marinade for 2 hours (time constraints) and could not grill today. I think it turns out great and moist in the oven. I dumped all the marinade in w/the thighs in a skillet with very tight lid. Part way thru cooking time I added chopped mushrooms, celery and cabbage. Also added chopped green onion. Was VERY GOOD!!!! Served with instant potatoes. Rice would have been great too, but am nearly out of my brown rice. Thanks so much for this recipe Wilemon :)

Really good! Made own teriyaki sauce: 1/2 c soy sauce, 1/4 c brown sugar, 1 1/2 tsp minced ginger; 1 tsp minced garlic, 1 T honey, 1 tsp sesame oil, 3 T white wine, 1/4 c water mixed w 3T corn starch. Combine, bring to boil and simmer for 4 minutes. Turn heat on grill down because it chars easily.

I added 1/2 tsp of fresh ginger & 1/2 tsp of sesame oil since I didn't have any liquid smoke. I also added 1 tsp of honey instead of brown sugar & 1 tblsp of sake. With so many spices & how could it not taste good! I also pan fried it in a hot iron skillet with the extra marinade added as needed since I soaked only 1 hr prior to cooking. With that much flavor in such a short time I can only imagine the full effect :)

Totally delicious! I used 1/2 of recipe--marinating 2 large Chix breasts overnight andcut down on garlic--use low sodium sauces. I then heated my stovetop grill pan very hot and grilled the breasts about 7 minutes on each side (turn down heat on each side last 2 minutes). Best, tender chicken I have eaten!
Next time I'll go lighter on liquid smoke, though I did marinate overnight. I baked @ 400F since it's beyond BBQ season here and it was yummy. Easy to put together and freezes well.

I mixed this exactly as written except I didn't have garlic pepper. So what I did was sub garlic powder and black pepper.

I have that FoodSaver Quick Marinator and used it with bone-in skin on thighs. Then cooked them in my air fryer.

Very nice flavor. Not sweet, not garlicky and not too smokey either. Will use this one again.
I tripled the recipe and it made 2 cups, so it makes about 2/3 cups as written.

Made per recipe and was definitely delectable! Always used to just throw several of the same ingredients in random amounts but definitely will use this recipe going forward! Probably just add some cayenne/sriracha next time to give it a little kick!
Very good marinade...I only added a teaspoon of finely grated ginger. Tasty with basmati rice.

I make this as written most of the time. Occasionally, I am out of sesame seeds, but it doesn't alter the taste at all. We LOVE this recipe and find any reason to make it. We have shared it with family and friends and it's always a BIG hit. Many people have asked me for the recipe. Thank you for sharing this.
Excellent recipe! My substitutions were 3 ounces IPA beer, extra fresh ground black pepper, 2 dashes salt, because I don’t have garlic salt or garlic pepper. Deeeelish!!
Amazing! All the perfect ingredients. This is a keeper and on the grill often.
This is my go to chicken thigh marinade for years. Alway a hit at gatherings and has never failed in someone asking for the recipe.
We love this recipe for chicken thighs. I have made it a number of times and the flavor is so good. It does not have the same profile for white meat, but the thighs are so yummy!
Really great recipe, the chicken was moist and tender. Definitely will make it again and again.
